questions.title: Top of the Stack
questions.description:
Warm up with the LIFO principle: the most recently pushed element is the top of the stack.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int stack_top(const int *stk, int top)

It must return stk[top], the value sitting on top of the stack (top is the index of the top element; the stack is never empty here).

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of pushed values.
Line 2: n space-separated integers, pushed in order.

Output Format:
One line with the top element.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, -1000 <= values <= 1000

questions.title: Pop Order of a Stack
questions.description:
Popping a stack emits the elements in reverse push order — practise that exact sequence.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void pop_order(const int *stk, int top, int *out)

It must fill out[0..top] with the pop sequence: out[j] = stk[top - j]. The harness prints out for you.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of pushed values.
Line 2: n space-separated integers, pushed in order.

Output Format:
One line with the n values in pop order, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, -1000 <= values <= 1000

questions.title: Peek the k-th Element from Top
questions.description:
Peeking looks at an element without popping it. Index 0 means the top of the stack.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int peek_k(const int *stk, int top, int k)

It must return stk[top - k], the element that is k positions below the top (0 <= k <= top).

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of pushed values.
Line 2: n space-separated integers, pushed in order.
Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the k-th element from the top.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, 0 <= k < n, -1000 <= values <= 1000

questions.title: Sum of Stack Elements
questions.description:
Traverse an array-based stack from bottom to top and add everything up.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int stack_sum(const int *stk, int top)

It must return the sum of stk[0..top].

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of pushed values.
Line 2: n space-separated integers, pushed in order.

Output Format:
One line with the sum.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, -1000 <= values <= 1000

questions.title: Balanced Round Brackets
questions.description:
The classic first application of a stack: check that every ( is closed by a matching ).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int is_balanced(const char *s)

It must return 1 when the string s (containing only '(' and ')') is balanced, and 0 otherwise. The harness prints YES or NO for you.

Input Format:
One token made only of '(' and ')' characters.

Output Format:
One line with YES or NO.

Constraints:
1 <= length of s <= 999

questions.title: Elements Remaining After Pops
questions.description:
Every pop removes exactly one element from the stack.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int remaining(int pushed, int popped)

It must return the number of elements still on the stack after popped successful pops.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: pushed and popped.

Output Format:
One line with the remaining count.

Constraints:
0 <= popped <= pushed <= 100000

questions.title: Text Editor Undo History
questions.description:
A text editor records every action code on an undo stack. Undo pops the most recent action.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int undo_top(const int *actions, int n, int undos)

It must return the action that ends up on top of the undo stack after undos undo steps, or -1 when every action has been undone.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of recorded actions.
Line 2: n action codes in the order they happened.
Line 3: undos.

Output Format:
One line with the resulting top action or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, 0 <= undos <= n, -1000 <= action codes <= 1000

questions.title: Browser Back Button
questions.description:
A browser pushes every visited page id onto a history stack. Pressing Back pops one page.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int current_page(const int *history, int n, int backs)

It must return the page id on top of the history after backs Back presses, or -1 when the history is exhausted (the user went back past the first page).

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of visited pages.
Line 2: n page ids in visiting order.
Line 3: backs.

Output Format:
One line with the current page id or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, 0 <= backs <= n, 1 <= page ids <= 100000

questions.title: Config File Bracket Linter
questions.description:
A linter validates configuration snippets that may mix round and square brackets; every opener needs the matching closer.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int brackets_ok(const char *s)

It must return 1 when every bracket in s (characters '(' ')' '[' ']') is properly matched and nested, and 0 otherwise. The harness prints YES or NO for you.

Input Format:
One token made only of '(' ')' '[' ']' characters.

Output Format:
One line with YES or NO.

Constraints:
1 <= length of s <= 999

questions.title: Next Greater Price (Single Query)
questions.description:
A price tracker answers one query: for a given day, what is the next strictly higher price after it?

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int next_greater_at(const int *arr, int n, int i)

It must return the first arr[j] with j > i and arr[j] > arr[i], or -1 if no such element exists.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated prices.
Line 3: i (0-based index).

Output Format:
One line with the next greater price or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, 0 <= i < n, -1000 <= prices <= 1000

questions.title: Next Greater Element for Every Item
questions.description:
A market data feed labels every price with the next strictly higher price that appears later in the list.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void next_greater(const int *arr, int n, int *out)

It must fill out[i] with the first arr[j] such that j > i and arr[j] > arr[i]; use -1 when no greater element exists. The harness prints the out array. A single left-to-right pass with a stack solves this in O(n).

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated values.

Output Format:
One line with n answers, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000 <= values <= 1000

questions.title: Valid Push and Pop Sequence
questions.description:
A warehouse robot logs push and pop commands. Verify the pop log could really have come from processing the push log with one stack (each sequence holds the same distinct values 1..n).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int valid_sequence(const int *pushed, const int *popped, int n)

It must return 1 if popped is a possible pop order of pushed, and 0 otherwise. The harness prints YES or NO.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n distinct values (the push order).
Line 3: n distinct values (the claimed pop order).

Output Format:
One line with YES or NO.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, each sequence is a permutation of 1..n
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 1000, each sequence is a permutation of 1..n

questions.title: Minimum on the Stack After Operations
questions.description:
A trading app replays a log of watchlist operations: a positive value v pushes price v, and -1 pops the most recent price. Report the minimum price still on the stack at the end (the final stack is never empty).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int min_after_ops(const int *ops, int m)

It must simulate the operations and return the minimum element on the stack after all of them. Track a running minimum alongside each push.

Input Format:
Line 1: m, the number of operations.
Line 2: m integers — each a positive value (push) or -1 (pop; pops never run on an empty stack).

Output Format:
One line with the minimum remaining element.

Constraints:
1 <= m <= 1000, 1 <= pushed values <= 100, the final stack is non-empty
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= m <= 1000, 1 <= pushed values <= 100, the final stack is non-empty

questions.title: Reverse a Message Using a Stack
questions.description:
A message de-obfuscator pushes every character onto a stack and then pops them all — which reads the text backwards.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void reverse_with_stack(const char *s, char *out)

It must push each character of s, then pop everything into out (reversed), and NUL-terminate out.

Input Format:
One token (no spaces).

Output Format:
One line with the reversed text.

Constraints:
1 <= length of s <= 999, s contains only printable non-space characters

questions.title: Minimum Bracket Removals
questions.description:
A log file contains a bracket string with some unmatched parentheses. Count the minimum number of brackets that must be removed to make it balanced.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int min_removals(const char *s)

It must return the total number of unmatched brackets: every '(' left unclosed plus every ')' with no opener.

Input Format:
One token made only of '(' and ')' characters.

Output Format:
One line with the count.

Constraints:
1 <= length of s <= 999

questions.title: Final Text After Backspaces
questions.description:
A keyboard driver records keystrokes where '#' means backspace. Replay the log with a stack of typed characters to reconstruct the final text.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void final_text(const char *s, char *out)

It must process s left to right: a normal character is pushed, '#' pops one character (ignored on an empty stack). Copy the surviving characters into out and NUL-terminate it.

Input Format:
One token of lowercase letters and '#'. At least one character survives.

Output Format:
One line with the final text.

Constraints:
1 <= length of s <= 999, the final text is non-empty
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= length of s <= 999, the final text is non-empty

questions.title: Postfix Expression Evaluator
questions.description:
A firmware calculator evaluates Reverse Polish Notation offline: operands are single digits 0-9 and operators are + - * / (integer division), all separated by single spaces.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int eval_postfix(const char *expr)

It must scan the tokens left to right, push operands, and on each operator pop b then pop a, compute a OP b, and push the result. Return the single value left on the stack. Division is integer division; b is never 0.

Input Format:
One line: a postfix expression with single-space-separated tokens.

Output Format:
One line with the evaluated value.

Constraints:
2 <= number of tokens <= 99, no division by zero
questions.inputconstrains: 2 <= number of tokens <= 99, no division by zero

questions.title: Stock Span Analysis
questions.description:
A trading dashboard shows, for each day, how many consecutive prior days (including today) had a price less than or equal to today's price — the stock span.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void stock_span(const int *prices, int n, int *out)

It must fill out[i] with the span of day i. A stack of indices solves this in O(n).

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated prices.

Output Format:
One line with n spans, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= prices <= 1000

questions.title: Circular Next Greater Element
questions.description:
A sensor ring wraps around: the element after the last one is the first one again. Compute the next strictly greater element for every position, searching circularly.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void nge_circular(const int *arr, int n, int *out)

It must fill out[i] with the next strictly greater value found by scanning forward (wrapping around once); use -1 when none exists.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n space-separated values.

Output Format:
One line with n answers, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000 <= values <= 1000

questions.title: Longest Valid Bracket Substring
questions.description:
A log-quality metric reports the length of the longest contiguous, fully balanced substring of parentheses in a log line.

The scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int longest_valid(const char *s)

It must return the length of the longest contiguous substring of s (characters '(' and ')') that is balanced; return 0 when none exists. A stack of indices (seeded with -1) solves this in one pass.

Input Format:
One token made only of '(' and ')' characters.

Output Format:
One line with the length.

Constraints:
1 <= length of s <= 999
